    Section 2

    Categorical Input Variables
    Reminder: Qualitative vs Quantitative predictors

    Quantitative:

    Qualitative/Categorical:

    Credit card balance

    • own: house ownership

    • student: student status

    • status: marital status

    • region: East, West, or South

    ... your variables aren’t quantitative?

    • Home ownership

    • Student status

    • Major

    • Gender

    • Ethnicity

    • Country of origin

    Example
    Investigate differences in credit card balance between people who own a house and those who don’t, ignoring the other variables.
    One-hot encoding of categorical input variable

    Create a new variable
    xi = { 1if ith person is a student 0 if ith person is not a student

    Model:

    yi = β0 + β1xi + εi = { β0 + β1 + εiif ith person is student β0 + εi if ith person isn’t
    Interpretation

    Model:
    y = 480.36 + 396.46 ⋅xstudent
    Who cares about 0/1?

    xi = { 1if ith person is a student 0 if ith person is not a student

    Section 3

    Extending the linear model
    Assumptions so far Back to our Advertising data set

    Ŷsales = β0 + β1 ⋅XTV + β2 ⋅Xradio + β3 ⋅Xnewspaper
    Assumed (implicitly) that the effect on sales by increasing one medium is independent of the others.
    What if spending money on radio advertising increases the effectiveness of TV advertising? How do we model it?
    Interaction Term

    Y = β0 + β1X1 + β2X2 + β3X1X2 + ε

    Y sales = β0 + β1XTV + β2Xradio + β3XradioXTV + ε = β0 + (β1 + β3Xradio)XTV + β2Xradio + ε = β0 + β1~XTV + β2Xradio + ε
    Interaction term

    Y = β0 + β1X1 + β2X2 + β3X1X2 + ε

    Y sales = β0 + β1XTV + β2Xradio + β3XradioXTV + ε = β0 + (β1 + β3Xradio)XTV + β2Xradio + ε
    Interpretation

    Hierarchy principle

    Sometimes p-value for interaction term is very small, but associated main effects are not.
    The hierarchy principle:
    Nonlinear relationships

    mpg = β0 + β1 ⋅horsepower + β2 ⋅horsepower2 + ε
